name: Charmine Rose Scalp Mezo Cocktail

lead: Scalp mezo cocktails are blends of vitamins, plant extracts and other ingredients delivered into the scalp by microinjection or needle-free devices. People use them hoping to improve hair thickness and scalp condition.
Charmine Rose is listed as a professional brand of such a product. Mesotherapy in general aims to nourish and hydrate skin.

paras: A clinician applies the product to the scalp in sessions, typically as a series.
Mesotherapy reports include skin abscesses and infections tied to unhygienic conditions, and swelling or inflammation depending on ingredients.

chain: Scalp environment is nourished and stimulated
angle.text: Users seek thicker-looking hair and a healthier scalp. Outcomes are discussed by practitioners; trial data on this specific product are absent.

lead: Charmine Rose Scalp Mezo Cocktail is a professional mesotherapy product aimed at the scalp. Mesotherapy involves intradermal or subcutaneous injection, or needle-free delivery, of substances such as vitamins, plant extracts, enzymes and hyaluronic acid to nourish and hydrate the skin.[1]

The technique originated with Michel Pistor, and the French Académie Nationale de Médecine recognised mesotherapy as a specialty in 1987.[1] Reviews report weak scientific support for cosmetic uses and note infection cases in clinics with poor hygiene.[1]

paras: Mesotherapy was credited to Michel Pistor (1924-2003); French media coined the term in 1958.[1] A study of 10 patients receiving facial multivitamin mesotherapy found no clinically relevant rejuvenation, and the technique is described as lacking proven clinical efficacy.[1]
Risks reported include abscesses in Australia and a mycobacterial infection; France briefly banned it for fat removal in 2011 before investigators attributed problems to unhygienic conditions.[1]
No studies found on this product.
